subject: Next steps: procurement path & packaging options for FinLogic
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finlogic.com>, Claire Watson <claire@finlogic.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: procurement path & packaging options for FinLogic

Hi Tom / Claire — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of what we heard
- Procurement preference: PO-driven for enterprise purchases; want to confirm internal approvals and billing cadence.
- Technical/regulatory: data residency for EU customers is a future ask, but current scope is US-hosted.
- Usage profile: spikey monthly usage with predictable baseline; priority is predictable unit cost and latency SLAs for production features.

Commercial paths to consider (high-level)
1) Hosted (Redwood API)
   - On-demand: pay-as-you-go card or invoice; lowest friction to start, ideal for proof-of-value.
   - Committed credits: 3/6/12 month commits with stepped discounts — reduces per-token cost and preferred if you can commit to baseline spend.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
   - Reserved GPU pools with monthly/annual commit; best for predictable high-throughput workloads and stricter isolation.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Enterprise install with platform fee + optional professional services; typically used when procurement or regulatory rules require customer-managed infra.

Procurement details we need from you
- Will the purchase go via PO or card? (PO required according to initial notes)
- Who is the budget owner and approver timeline?
- Do you prefer an AWS Marketplace route (we can list to simplify procurement) or a direct contract with Redwood?
- Any standard PO terms or CLA/contract redlines we should review early?

Attachments: initial-quote-hosted-dedicated.pdf, procurement-checklist.xlsx (first-pass numbers and a short checklist for your procurement team).

Suggested next steps
- Could we schedule a 30-min follow-up with procurement/legal next week to review the PO template and a pricing summary?
- I'll prepare a short pricing comparison (on-demand vs commit vs dedicated), plus a Marketplace setup note if you want that path.

Thanks — I’ll wait for a quick note on PO vs card and a suggested time for the procurement sync.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finlogic.com>

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement path & packaging options for FinLogic

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement preference: We will require a PO for anything > $10k per invoice. Card is only for low-dollar POCs.
- Timeline: Budget owner approval target mid-April (finance lead out 3/23, will resume approvals after).
- Marketplace: We are interested in AWS Marketplace — that typically shortens the internal procurement path here. Can you confirm if Redwood supports Metered Billing via Marketplace or if you use private offers?
- Commit questions: what are the minimums for committed credits and the typical discount bands for 3/6/12 months? Also any minimum guaranteed throughput for Dedicated?
- Data residency: For now US-only is OK, but we'd like a note on options if we move to EU later.

Attaching our PO template: FinLogic-PO-template.docx. Please send a version of the quote that fits that template so procurement can review.

Tom Lee
Head of Procurement | FinLogic
Tom.Lee@finlogic.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement path & packaging options for FinLogic

Tom — great, thanks for the clarity and the PO template. Quick answers and what I’ll send you today: 

Procurement / billing options
- PO: we can invoice on Net30/Net45 depending on credit approval; PO-driven purchases are supported and standard for Dedicated/Private.
- Marketplace: Redwood supports listing in AWS Marketplace; we can do Metered Billing or Private Offers depending on which accelerates your buying. I’ll include the Marketplace setup note.

Pricing summary (I will attach the detailed spreadsheet)
- Hosted on-demand: list price (no commit) — lowest startup friction.
- Hosted committed credits: discount bands typically at ~10% (3mo), ~18% (6mo), ~25% (12mo) depending on volume; we’ll show the math on your expected usage profile.
- Dedicated: pricing is based on reserved GPU capacity and has an annual or monthly commit; recommended if you need consistent latency and isolated capacity.
- Private: enterprise license + professional services; longer lead time for deployment and separate procurement.

Next steps I’m taking now
- Convert the initial quote into your PO template and attach a pricing-summary-v1.xlsx with commit scenarios.
- Include redwood-marketplace-setup.pdf that outlines Metered vs Private Offer paths and implications for billing cadence.
- Propose a 30-min call with your procurement on Tue 10 Mar at 11am ET — does that time work for you?

Attachments: redwood-marketplace-setup.pdf, pricing-summary-v1.xlsx (pricing scenarios and commit math).

If approved, we can also prep a draft SOW and a DocuSign envelope to accelerate signatures once PO terms are finalized.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
